correctness.rationale: Colour exchange makes the fixed m=floor(N/2) choice exact for W_n. A disconnected colour implies that its complement is connected, so k-1 cross-component edges are necessary and sufficient when the disconnected colour has k components. A specified cut of a edges is empty with probability at most 2^(-a)(1+1/N)^a ≤ e·2^(-a). Two isolates use a=2n-3; a component of size two uses a=2(n-2); cuts of sizes 3 through floor(n/2) contribute at most e·2^n·2^(-3(n-3)). Thus the non-singleton exceptional probability is O(n²4^(-n)), and the expectation differs from the isolate expectation by at most O(n³4^(-n)). In the normalized central product log, the first three power sums give -1+(2-2)/n+(5-14/3)/n²+O(n^(-3)), and the higher powers sum to O(n^(-3)). For the half-integer shifts, the symmetric average of the two factors cancels odd terms; the quadratic term is δ²(A²-B)/2 with A=4/n+O(n^(-2)) and B=O(n^(-3)). This gives 2ε_n/n², so the parity-resolved coefficients are correct. Independent log-product replay gives scaled coefficients 0.3367039875 and 2.3566886531 at n=300 and 302, tracking 1/3 and 7/3 respectively; only the proof establishes the bounds on the graph events.
residual_risks: The replay checks the isolate product, not a numerical test of the tail or all-n error estimates.

evidence: Dawkins et al. show qualitative decay of the expectation in the same equitable model. Bender–Canfield–McKay give asymptotic connected-graph counts in the fixed-edge model; the inspected abstract and theorem discussion concern the connected count, not a law distinguishing W=1 and W≥2. The indexed rare-event theorem states the same W≥2 bound and also gives P(W=0).
broader_coverage.reasoning: Qualitative decay alone is not coverage. The indexed rare-event theorem is strictly stronger in this regime because of the exact leading term and its smaller additive errors.
